summary: The University of Arizona's neuroscience PhD program, admitting for fall. First-year students are supported by the program while they take courses and rotate through labs.
detailsNote: Official information available; the December 1 deadline has no year stated, so Fall 2027 is not confirmed. The application page still mentions sending GRE scores, but the requirements page says the GRE is no longer required.

publishedDeadlines.label: Published application deadline (no year stated)
publishedDeadlines.note: The how-to-apply page says 'The deadline for applications is December 1st.' No year, time or time zone is given. Confirm Fall 2027 directly.

timeline.interviews: Interviews typically begin late January for fall admission.

english.note: For international students, from the Program in Neuroscience requirements page. International students should also provide at least one letter from a scientist who knows the US system.

applicationFee.note: Same fee ($90) for international students. 'Fee waived on case by case based upon request.' The page does not say who qualifies; confirm.

requirements.note: The program describes a strong application as a GPA of 3.5 or higher with a research background, but sets no absolute GPA cutoff.

funding.note: Page: 'All students in good standing in the Program of Neuroscience receive financial support in the form of an annual stipend.' Stipend shown is Level 1 in the 2026-27 example table (Level 2 is $34,350). Non-Arizona residents get an out-of-state tuition waiver; student health plan is covered. Visa holders are not eligible for NRSA support.
